title: Master Excel Dynamic Arrays (Excel 365)
description: Learn how to use modern dynamic array functions like FILTER, SORT, UNIQUE, and SEQUENCE to transform your spreadsheets.
intro: Dynamic arrays are one of the most significant updates to Excel in recent years. They automatically spill results into multiple cells, eliminating the need for Ctrl+Shift+Enter array formulas. Functions like FILTER, SORT, UNIQUE, and SEQUENCE make complex data manipulation simple and intuitive.
prerequisites: Excel 365 or Excel 2021 (dynamic arrays not available in older versions)

sections.title: Understanding Dynamic Arrays
sections.content: Dynamic arrays automatically spill results into adjacent cells. When you enter a formula that returns multiple values, Excel places each value in a separate cell.

steps.name: Spill behavior
steps.text: Dynamic array formulas return arrays that 'spill' to fill as many cells as needed.

steps.name: #SPILL! error
steps.text: If there's already data in the spill range, you'll get a #SPILL! error.

tips: Dynamic arrays work in Excel 365, Excel 2021, and Google Sheets.
You can reference a spill range with the # operator.

sections.title: FILTER Function
sections.content: FILTER extracts rows from a range that meet specified conditions.

example.result: All rows where Column B equals 'Sales'
example.explanation: Filters the range A2:C100 to show only rows where Column B contains 'Sales'.

sections.title: SORT Function
sections.content: SORT sorts a range by specified columns.

example.result: Data sorted by Column C in descending order
example.explanation: Sorts the range A2:C100 by the 3rd column (C) in descending order (-1).

tips: Sort by multiple columns by providing an array of column numbers.

sections.title: UNIQUE Function
sections.content: UNIQUE returns unique values from a range, removing duplicates.

example.result: All unique values in Column A
example.explanation: Returns each value from A2:A100 only once, even if it appears multiple times.

tips: Use UNIQUE with multiple columns to find unique combinations.
Add TRUE as the second argument to compare case-sensitively.

sections.title: SEQUENCE Function
sections.content: SEQUENCE generates a sequence of numbers.

example.explanation: Generates a 10-row, 1-column sequence starting at 1, incrementing by 1.

tips: Great for creating numbered lists or date sequences.

sections.title: Combining Dynamic Array Functions
sections.content: The real power comes from combining these functions.

example.result: Sales data sorted by amount descending
example.explanation: Filters for sales records, then sorts by column 3 (amount) from highest to lowest.

tips: Use UNIQUE(SORT(FILTER(...))) for unique sorted filtered results.

summary: Dynamic array functions are a game-changer for Excel users. FILTER, SORT, UNIQUE, and SEQUENCE make complex data manipulation much simpler without the need for array formulas. By combining these functions, you can create powerful data analysis workflows that update automatically when your source data changes.
